interventions.what: Bandicam window capture of the Isle Wars Pro game window; the owner played one game from the options screen to the end screen (15:10 recording). The video file is the only output. No scripted clicks. Counters, seats and screens were read from pixels by region comparison and template matching of glyph shapes, with no OCR pass.

start_state.restore: Owner launched a new game on the unregistered Pro build from the options screen (seat 1 human, three computer seats, starting level set to the easy entry and game speed to the slow entry). Pro has no save file (C-SET-05), so no state was restored. The recording starts on the title screen; the opening deal is the first board.

observations.field: human placement summary
observations.value: eight placements in eight human turns, the whole pool each time on one country (no split), stacks after placement 7, 8, 12, 13, 17, 27, 41 and 26 (the last on a country that held 1; 1 plus 25); the pool is 4 to 27. The owner built exact stacks of 8 (turn 5, country 42) and 12 (turn 9, country 43) and attacked from stacks of 12, 13, 17, 27, 41 and 34 later, but every defender held 1 to 4 armies, so no even or underdog cell of E021 was reached (see the sitting's section).

observations.value: source held 7 armies; counters before and after: source 7 to 1, destination 1 to 7; moved 6, kept 1; the move counter read 1 at 02:13.2 and 6 at 02:15.0 (the way it was set, all-but-one button or up button, was not isolated: intermediate values were not read); source and destination both blue and neighbours; the move came after the last attack of the turn (attack 4 at 02:01.9); after confirm the draw screen of the turn came within 2 s (a joker draw), then the next seat.

observations.field: move summary
observations.value: four completed human moves in eight human turns (turns 5, 13, 21, 25), at most one per turn, each after the turn's last attack and ending the turn (the draw screen followed within 2 s); every move left exactly 1 in the source (sources of 7, 6, 12 and 26 armies; moves of 6, 5, 11 and 25: all but one, the largest all-but-one so far, a stack of 26); the all-but-one button was shown highlighted for moves 3 and 4, the up button for move 2; two moves were started and cancelled (turn 13 at 05:02.4 and turn 21 at 10:52.4, both by the cancel button of the destination prompt, after choosing a source), and the owner started a move again each time; a third cancelled order was an attack target prompt (turn 21, 10:56.0 to 10:58.0). No computer move was detected by the left-panel template that found 5 in IP1 028 and 7 in IP1 027.
